newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate ends higher on stock gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate ends higher on stock gains.

text.p: Taiwan's interbank rate closed higher on Thursday as funds continued to stream out of the banking system into the red hot stock market, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 7.418 percent against Wednesday's 7.208 close -- outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone but still far below the double-digit closes of late June.
The 30-day commercial paper was at 7.25-7.75 percent against 7.50-7.75.
The stock market on Thursday closed 67.06 points or 0.72 percent higher to set a seven-year high of 9,429.74.
Turnover in the stock market was extremely heavy at T$220 billion, which dealers said intensified cash demand in the money market.
But dealers said the money rates likely would stabilise at the current levels if the central bank opted not to launch further tightening measures.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.0000-0025 percent against 5.9775-9800.
